key_insight: Post-deletion accuracy alone can be misleading for materials machine unlearning, so the paper defines a “deletion floor” as the retraining loss baseline and bounds how much a deletion update can deviate from it.
engineering_relevance: For property prediction models in materials science, unlearning should be judged relative to what retraining leaves behind, not just by whether the deleted sample is hard to predict.
method: Defines the deletion floor: expected target loss under a specified retraining procedure at the deleted request.
Derives sharp indistinguishability-based bounds on an update’s target loss around that baseline.
Provides a conditional neighbor bound and an exact ridge identity linking retrained fit, prediction regularity, and deletion-induced change.
evidence_signal: Experiments report an approximately 8× drop in median normalized retraining loss when one retained relative remains after deletion, and a paired Materials Project study shows the lower-floor regime has larger prediction changes on more than 50% of shared requests.
watch_item: The deletion floor depends on the chosen retraining procedure, so comparisons across methods must keep the retraining reference and evaluation protocol consistent.
paper_title: Bounding Retraining Equivalence and the Deletion Floor in Materials Machine Unlearning
